Maya P.: Quick sync — we need a locked, reproducible methodology for one-to-one model comparisons (kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV warm/cold behavior, tokenizer alignment, decoding params). Can we finalize a checklist today?

Ryan L.: +1. Found a surprising p99 regression in last runtime build when the fused MLP kernel was selected automatically. p50 unchanged but p99 +5%. I can share perf traces.

Samir B.: Can you drop the trace? Likely the batching heuristic triggered larger micro-batches for some seq lengths. Quick config I want to try:
```yaml
batcher:
  mode: adaptive
  max_batch_size: 8
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  latency_slo_ms: 80
  warmup_cooldown_ms: 200
```
This forces earlier flush on latency-sensitive routes.

Maya P.: Good call. Also propose we standardize on: same prompt set (fixed seed draw from prod-like replay), identical decoding params (temp=0, top_p=0.95 for sampling tests or temp=0 for deterministic), same stop sequences, same max_new_tokens, and identical tokenizer+preproc. We should run both synthetic traffic (uniform RTT/arrival) and replay harness (real traces) for each run.

Lisa H.: Tokenizer alignment notes:
- Use the same tokenizer binary/version where possible.
- If models use different tokenizers, run canonicalization: normalize unicode, strip/keep spaces consistently, and run a token-diff pass.
- Stop sequences must be applied post-detokenize in the same way (avoid model-specific auto-truncation).
Example check command:
```bash
python tools/tokenizer_check.py --prompts tests/replay_prompts.txt --tok-a out/modelA_tok.json --tok-b out/modelB_tok.json --report tok-diff.csv
```
This outputs token counts and mismatches per prompt.

Ryan L.: From the perf traces: KV cache warmup gives ~12–18ms improvement for avg 64-token continuation on GPU A100-40GB when cached keys hit. For cold-run we need to record both cold and warmed p50/p95/p99. I ran a quick run:
p50: 22ms (warm), 34ms (cold)
p95: 48ms (warm), 92ms (cold)
p99: 120ms (warm), 210ms (cold)
Also repro steps: set ENV MODEL_KERNEL_OVERRIDE="auto|mlp-fused|mlp-ref" and run harness to see kernel impact.

Samir B.: For the harness invocation I recommend this canonical command (deterministic sampling where needed):
```bash
REPLAY_PROMPTS=tests/3000_prompts.json \nMODEL_A=redwood/curie-quant \nMODEL_B=open/curie-ref \npython tools/replay_compare.py \n  --seed 42 \n  --decode "temp=0.0 top_p=0.95 max_new_tokens=128" \n  --batcher config/batcher_adaptive.yaml \n  --record-profiles /tmp/profiles/${THREAD_ID}.json
```
Include environment flags to pin kernel selection for controlled experiments.

Maya P.: Action items: 1) Ryan to post the full trace + pprof links (due EOD). 2) Samir to land a batcher config that enforces latency SLOs for the comparison runs. 3) Lisa to run tokenizer_check across the prompt seed and produce tok-diff.csv. 4) I will run a 3x repeat for synthetic and replay runs and collect p50/p95/p99 + token-level diffs.
